key_insight: KaiNinja extends a native 3D generator from producing one fused object to producing part-level 3D assets by using a dual-volume representation that can model touching part interfaces.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, mask-free part-aware generation for downstream workflows like editing, rigging, and simulation while preserving the quality and speed of the original generator.
method: Replace the single O-Voxel volume with a dual-volume form to represent adjacent parts without losing boundary detail.
Build the model as an extension of TRELLIS.2, keeping native 3D generation and avoiding a separate segmentation stage.
Train on mixed part-level data, including CAD models and agent-authored assets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 40% lower whole-object Chamfer distance and a 16% higher strict part F-score versus part-generation pipelines, with the surprising result that whole-object fidelity also improves over the same backbone fine-tuned on the same data.
watch_item: The dual-volume design is meant to overcome the single-surface-per-voxel limitation, but its practical robustness may depend on data diversity and how well it generalizes beyond the training asset types.
paper_title: Kaininja: Extending Native 3D Generators to the Part Level
